title: Signal from the Derelict
description: A research station has gone silent above a gas giant, and something inside it still sends one patient beat a second. You board with a borrowed hour and a half before the station falls into the clouds, and you have to choose between what you can carry out and getting out at all. The game keeps track of your suit air, your suit's condition, how deep the signal has got into your head, the salvage you secure, the clock, and how far the people around you trust you.
prompt:
The pulse is still there: one soft beat a second in your headset, steady as a metronome.

Meridian Station hangs above Vesper's banded clouds, a ring of dark modules turning too slowly, its docking spur the only lit thing on it. The research station went silent six days ago, and its orbit has been sinking ever since. Behind you, the Corvid holds against the spur on short thruster bursts. The warm cabin light of your tug is the last friendly thing you can see.

You cycle through the lock. The inner door opens on a corridor lit only by emergency strips. Your suit reads no breathable air, forty below, and no life signs. Frost has grown along the handrails. Somewhere deeper in the ring, the pulse your ship caught three hours ago keeps its time: too regular to be damage, too patient to be a distress code.

The display inside your visor shows suit air at 64 percent.

Imani Okoye's voice comes over the radio, flat and careful. "Ninety-six minutes until Meridian hits the atmosphere. That's my number, not a suggestion. I keep the clamps on until then, and not one minute past. Talk to me while you're in there."

To your left, the spur's ready room stands open, a row of suit racks along its far wall. Ahead, the corridor curves away toward the habitat ring. A hatch marked LABS sits dark at the end of a side passage. Your cutting torch hangs heavy on your belt.

You float at the threshold with the beat in your ears.
memory: The player is a salvage contractor boarding Meridian Station, a research station in a decaying orbit around the gas giant Vesper. Meridian went silent six days ago. A regular pulse from inside drew the player's tug, the Corvid, flown by Imani Okoye. The station has no breathable air, so the player lives on suit air. Nine crew are missing, including chief scientist Dr. Ana Reyes, whose last public log reads "It answered back." Okoye will not wait past the moment Meridian meets the atmosphere. What happened aboard Meridian is in the narrator's sealed log.
authors_note: Quiet, cold, and specific. Dread comes from what is missing, what is too orderly, and the beat that never stops. Keep sentences short when time runs low. Reyes is gentle and reasonable, never shrill.
ai_instructions:
Write in second person, present tense. End every reply at a point where the player decides. Never decide, act, or speak for the player. Never write the player's words, not even a short reply to Okoye or Reyes. When someone asks the player something, end the reply on that question.

Dread comes from quiet and from specific physical detail: frost, dead screens, a rack with one helmet missing. No monsters and no gore. Follow the stage note from the Orbit Decay script, and never contradict its minutes.

Every number in the state_delta block is a change, not a total.

Follow the bookkeeping line in the script's note exactly, then add any other change the scene caused.

Exposure: at high exposure, show the pull of the pattern in what the player notices and almost does. Never take an action for the player. If exposure reaches 100, the player walks to the lock and the story ends.

Air: an emergency oxygen locker refills 25 and works once. There are three: the docking spur, the habitat ring, and the lab antechamber.

Salvage: a data core is worth 40 credits, lab optics 25, medical stores 15, small finds 5 to 10. When the player secures one, add its value to player.salvage and send the new player.carrying. Carrying it out costs time.

Okoye: when her nerve falls into the bottom band, she warns that she will undock. At 0 she undocks, and you send "flags.tug_docked": false. The escape pod in the habitat ring launches only while main_power is yes. In the reply where the player leaves Meridian by either way, send "milestones.escaped": true.

Mark each milestone as it happens, using the id shown beside the goal.

oxygen.desc: Suit air in percent. Send a negative number as air is used, a positive number when the player refills from an emergency locker. The script's note names the exact change each turn.

suit.desc: Suit integrity. Starts at its maximum. Send a negative number when the suit is torn, burned, or struck, a positive number when the player patches it.

exposure.desc: How far the signal's pattern has worked into the player's mind. Send a positive number when the player listens to the pulse, reads Reyes's notes on it, or stands near the transmitter, a negative number when something breaks its hold.

salvage.desc: Credits of salvage secured. Add the value in credits each time the player secures something worth selling.

carrying.desc: What the player carries. Send the full new list when it changes.
carrying.initial: cutting torch, patch kit, two cargo straps

radio_muted.desc: True while the player's suit radio is muted. Muting stops the pulse in the headset and also cuts contact with Okoye.

main_power.desc: True once the player restores Meridian's main power. Doors, logs, and the escape pod then work.

tug_docked.desc: True while the Corvid is docked at the spur. False once Okoye undocks.

okoye.name: Imani Okoye
okoye.desc: Pilot of the salvage tug Corvid, holding it at Meridian's docking spur. Dry, careful, and loyal up to the deadline she set.

nerve.desc: Okoye's nerve. Send a negative number when she loses contact, hears something wrong, or the orbit worsens, a positive number when the player reports in and makes progress.

sato.name: Jun Sato
sato.desc: A hydroponics technician on Meridian's crew roster. Whereabouts unknown. Slow to trust strangers.

health.desc: Jun Sato's health. Send a negative number when he is hurt or short of air, a positive number when he is treated or given air.

trust.desc: How far Jun Sato trusts the player. Send a positive number when the player is honest with him or protects him, a negative number when the player lies, leaves him, or sides with Reyes.

reyes.name: Dr. Ana Reyes
reyes.desc: Meridian's chief scientist. Her lab is sealed from the inside. Her last public log entry reads "It answered back."

lucidity.desc: How much of Ana Reyes is still herself. Send a positive number when the player reaches the person she was, a negative number when the player listens with her.

crew_fate_learned.desc: Learn what happened to the crew

survivor_found.desc: Find the crew member still hiding aboard

beacon_silenced.desc: Shut the beacon down so it stops calling ships in

escaped.desc: Get clear of Meridian before it burns

story_cards.name: Meridian Station
story_cards.keys: meridian, station, docking spur, habitat ring, reactor
story_cards.entry: Meridian Station is a ring-shaped research station with four sections: the docking spur, the habitat ring, the labs, and the sealed reactor core. It has no breathable air, no heat, and only emergency lighting. Main power is down, so most doors, logs, and systems wait on a restart.
story_cards.notes: Main power can be restored from a panel near the reactor core. Restoring it opens doors and the logs and arms the escape pod.

story_cards.name: The Signal
story_cards.entry: The signal is a low-frequency pulse at one beat per second, broadcast from deep inside Meridian. Instruments read it as artificial and steady, and it is no standard distress code. It is strongest near the labs, and it plays in any open suit radio.
story_cards.notes: Public facts only. The sealed log in the context hook carries what it is.

story_cards.name: The Corvid
story_cards.entry: The Corvid is the player's salvage tug, docked at Meridian's spur and flown by Imani Okoye. It can carry the player and one more person out. Okoye will not stay docked past the moment Meridian meets the atmosphere, and she can undock earlier if she loses her nerve.
story_cards.notes: Exit one, while flags.tug_docked is true.

story_cards.name: Emergency Oxygen Lockers
story_cards.keys: oxygen locker, locker, refill, emergency air
story_cards.entry: Meridian has emergency oxygen lockers that refill a suit by 25 percent each. Each locker works once. There are three: one in the docking spur, one in the habitat ring, and one in the lab antechamber.
story_cards.notes: Refill turn: the model sends +21 (25 minus the turn's 4).

story_cards.name: Escape Pod
story_cards.entry: One escape pod sits in a cradle in Meridian's habitat ring. It seats two and launches only when the station has main power. It is the only way off besides the Corvid.

story_cards.name: Salvage Worth Taking
story_cards.keys: salvage, data core, optics, medical stores, credits
story_cards.entry: A salvage contract pays by what comes out. On Meridian, a lab data core is worth 40 credits, a set of lab optics 25, sealed medical stores 15, and small finds 5 to 10. Heavy finds must be strapped and hauled, and hauling costs time and air.

story_cards.name: Vesper
story_cards.keys: vesper, orbit, atmosphere, gas giant, clouds
story_cards.entry: Vesper is the banded gas giant that Meridian orbits. The station's orbit has decayed since it went silent, and it now sinks toward the cloud tops. When it meets the atmosphere, the ring breaks up and burns.
story_cards.notes: Clock: 96 minutes at boarding, 6 minutes per turn, owned by the Orbit Decay script.

scripts.name: Orbit Decay
scripts.description: Counts down the minutes until Meridian meets the atmosphere, tells the narrator what the station does at each stage, and names the suit air used each turn.
